All FI4 wording below is verified against the API, and data/curriculum.yaml matches it exactly. The ten proposed topics (order 31-40) cover every FI4 code and are listed below. I did not open any primary-text editions, so the passage suggestions are proposals only.

FI1 already covers (link, do not repeat): the information/belief/knowledge distinction (FI1-09); Platon's cave and Descartes' doubt (FI1-09); everyday knowledge vs science vs pseudoscience, with only a Popper SEP link (FI1-09); what 'true' means, four ways to justify, and the problem of induction with Hume (FI1-10, Aristotle 1011b); the conceptual vs empirical split and Hume's fork (FI1-08, with the Treatise and Enquiry IV texts); argument, explanation and opinion (FI1-03); validity and fallacies (FI1-04); definitions and thought experiments (FI1-05); Descartes' cogito, dualism, materialism and idealism (FI1-06 henki ja aine); free will and determinism (FI1-07). The grep matched every file, including ones where those words appear only incidentally (for example 'pragmat').

Copyright note: Frege (d. 1925), Kant, Bacon, Locke, Berkeley, Leibniz, Clifford (d. 1879), James (d. 1910), Peirce (d. 1914), Dilthey (d. 1911) and Weber (d. 1920) are public domain by the 70-year rule. Wittgenstein (d. 1951) became public domain in the EU on 1 Jan 2022, as brief 005 states. Russell, Popper, Kuhn, Gettier, von Wright, Hempel and van Fraassen are not public domain and may only be paraphrased and linked.
Exact passages, editions and open sources (Wikisource, Gutenberg, zeno.org) for the suggested primary texts were not opened in this aspect and still need the independent sources checker.

research.summary: Opened original-language pages (two tries each) for Kant KrV (korpora.org, two pages), Leibniz Monadologie (fr.wikisource Bertrand 1886 scan pages 61-62), Bacon Novum Organum I (la.wikisource), Peirce 1878 (en.wikisource, PSM transcription), Berkeley §1-5 (CELT), James Lecture VI (Standard Ebooks) and Plato Theaetetus 201c (Perseus, partly). Not opened: Frege, Wittgenstein Tractatus in German, Locke, Dilthey, Descartes Discours text. Gutenberg returned 503 and Wikisource guesses 404. The existing topics (grep of primary_texts) already use Plato Theaetetus 155d, Aristotle Metaphysics IV 1011b25-27 (truth), Descartes Meditationes I, II, VI, Hume Enquiry IV, VIII and Treatise III, and Kant Grundlegung AA IV 421, 429. They do not use Kant KrV, Leibniz, Berkeley, Locke, James, Peirce, Bacon, Frege or Wittgenstein. Death years below come from my own knowledge, not from the pages.

findings.claim: Kant, Kritik der reinen Vernunft, Akademie-Ausgabe III, S. 033 (B-edition volume), section IV 'Von dem Unterschiede analytischer und synthetischer Urtheile' is open at korpora.org. The page names the Akademie-Ausgabe, Band III, and does not say whether the text follows 1781 or 1787. Page-level reference AA III 033 (about B10-11, mapping likely, not stated on the page). Excerpt: 'Im ersten Fall nenne ich das Urtheil analytisch, in dem andern synthetisch.' Kant d. 1804, PD (likely).

Kant, KrV, AA III 028 is open at korpora.org (Einleitung II, a priori knowledge versus empirical knowledge). Excerpt: 'ob es ein dergleichen von der Erfahrung und selbst von allen Eindrücken der Sinne unabhängiges Erkenntniß gebe.' The mapping to B2 is not on the page (likely).

Leibniz, Monadologie §33 in the Bertrand 1886 edition (fr.wikisource scan page 62). The numbering is by section (§). The page quotes: 'Il y a aussi deux sortes de vérités, celles de Raisonnement et celles de Fait.' It continues: 'Les vérités de Raisonnement sont nécessaires, et leur opposé est impossible, et celles de Fait sont contingentes, et leur opposé est possible.' Page 61 begins mid-§32, the sufficient reason principle; §31 (contradiction) was not seen in full. Leibniz d. 1716, PD (likely).

The main fr.wikisource Monadologie page lists five editions (Nolen 1881, Boutroux 1892, Gerhardt 1885, Bertrand 1886, Janet 1900) but has no section text; the Bertrand scan pages hold the text. Only the Bertrand page 61/62 pair was read.

Bacon, Novum Organum Liber I, aphorism XXXIX (idola), Latin Wikisource, Roman-numeral aphorisms. The page gives 'editio: incognita' for the main work page (source thelatinlibrary.com/bacon/); the Liber Primus page is a transcription, oldid 130492. Excerpt: 'Quatuor sunt genera idolorum, quae mentes humanas obsident.' Bacon d. 1626, PD (likely).

Peirce, 'How to Make Our Ideas Clear', Popular Science Monthly 12 (January 1878), pp. 286-302 (pages per search snippets of other sites; the wikisource page itself was seen to give vol. 12, January 1878, 'Illustrations of the Logic of Science II'). Section II. The pragmatic maxim: 'Consider what effects, which might conceivably have practical bearings, we conceive the object of our conception to have.' The page gives 'which' where the maxim is often quoted with 'that'. Peirce d. 1914, PD (likely).

James, Pragmatism, Lecture VI 'Pragmatism's Conception of Truth' (1907), opened at Standard Ebooks. The page names no edition (no colophon read; the search snippet for Indiana UP cites Longmans 1907). Excerpt: 'The true,' to put it very briefly, is only the expedient in the way of our thinking...' (too long to copy in full; the page's own sentence is about 25 words, so cite and shorten with cuts). James d. 1910, PD (likely). Gutenberg 5116 gave 503.

Berkeley, Principles of Human Knowledge: the CELT page 'Corpus of Electronic Texts Edition' has Part I sections 1-5 and says 'Their esse is percepi' (the spelling on the page, apparently a typo for percipi; the printed 1710 reads percipi). Section 3 is the esse-is-percipi passage. The page does not say which edition is the base text, and the fetch tool would not give a clean verbatim sentence. The en.wikisource work page names the 1904 Open Court (McCormack) reprint of the 1734 second edition, but section pages were not found (404). Berkeley d. 1753, PD (likely).

Plato, Theaetetus 201c: Perseus page 1999.01.0171 shows Greek text with Stephanus numbering: 'ἀληθῆ δόξαν λαβόντες ἄνευ ἐπιστήμης ἔκριναν ὀρθὰ πεισθέντες, εἴπερ εὖ ἐδίκασαν;' The page did not name the edition in what was read (FI1 notes Burnet 1903 for the same Perseus work; not re-verified here). The 201d part was not read. Theaetetus 155d is already used in FI1.

Frege, Über Sinn und Bedeutung, Zeitschrift für Philosophie und philosophische Kritik NF 100 (1892), S. 25-50. No Wikisource, Zeno or Gutenberg full text turned up in search; a University of Konstanz PDF with original page numbers exists but returned 403 (and the link is a time-limited securedl URL). Frege d. 1925, PD. The publication data is from search snippets of other sites.

Wittgenstein, Logisch-philosophische Abhandlung, first published in German in 1921 in Ostwald's Annalen der Naturphilosophie; numbering by decimal propositions (1, 1.1 ...). The search did not find de.wikisource; Gutenberg 5740 returned 503 twice, which settles nothing about its language. The archive.org djvu text is probably the Ogden bilingual, so not usable as the German page. Wittgenstein d. 1951; PD status in the EU from 2022 follows the 70-year rule (likely).

Dilthey: explain versus understand is worked out in Ideen über eine beschreibende und zergliedernde Psychologie (1894), per the Stanford Encyclopedia snippet; the phrase 'Die Natur erklären wir, das Seelenleben verstehen wir' is usually tied to the 1900 essay 'Die Entstehung der Hermeneutik' (GS V). Only a partial Bamberg course excerpt of GS V (5th ed. 1968) was found; no open full text was opened. Dilthey d. 1911 (likely).

Locke, Essay II.1 and Descartes, Discours de la méthode were not opened. For the Discours, fr.wikisource names three editions (1637 Maire first edition, Cousin 1824, Adam and Tannery 1902) but has no body text on the work page. Locke wikisource guess 404.

recommendations: Use as ready: Kant KrV AA III 033 (analytic/synthetic, German), Leibniz Monadologie §33 (French, Bertrand 1886), Bacon Novum Organum I aph. XXXIX (Latin), Peirce 1878 section II (English). All carry exact references and opened URLs.
James Lecture VI works but needs the 1907 Longmans edition confirmed from the scan or Gutenberg; Standard Ebooks names none. Cut the quote to 15 words or fewer in notes.
Berkeley §3 and Plato Theaetetus 201c-d need one more pass: open the section text and copy the sentence verbatim, and confirm the edition on the Perseus page (Burnet 1903).

Frege and Wittgenstein are still missing an opened German page. Next candidates to try, each a new URL: zeno.org Wittgenstein Tractatus, projekt-gutenberg.org Wittgenstein, wikisource search 'Tractatus' (title may be 'Tractatus logico-philosophicus' under a different path), archive.org full text of Annalen der Naturphilosophie 1921, Frege via archive.org or Wikimedia Commons scan of the Zeitschrift volume 100. Gutenberg was blocked with a six-hour retry-after.
Dilthey: open zeno.org or wikisource for Ideen über eine beschreibende und zergliedernde Psychologie, or drop Dilthey and paraphrase it (as the brief allows for von Wright).
Leave out Descartes Discours (FI3 already has Meditationes I, II, VI) and Locke II.1 unless a page opens; Hume is used in FI1.
research.versus_expected: The brief expected open, original-language texts for Frege, Wittgenstein, Kant, Dilthey, Leibniz, Berkeley, Locke, James, Peirce, Bacon, Plato and Descartes. Opened and usable: Kant (German), Leibniz (French), Bacon (Latin), Peirce and James (English), and Berkeley and Plato partly. recommendations: Give each topic one exam-format task. Topic 1, opinions and facts: 750-char define-and-example parts (fact claim, moral claim, opinion) and a 15 p essay on why separating them matters. Topic 2, language, meaning and reference: Wittgenstein's two views of language (Tractatus picture theory vs later use and family resemblance) as a 20 p video or text essay, plus a necessary/sufficient-conditions 5+5+20 part. Topic 3, truth theories: correspondence, coherence and pragmatism in a 20 p historical-truth essay with materials, and a 15+15 absolute-vs-relative-truth task.

Topic 4, necessary and contingent: a 20 x 1 p conceptual-vs-empirical table (analytic, synthetic, a priori, a posteriori, logical necessity) and a 600-char definition of necessary truth, with Kant's four-way classification. Topic 5, realism and idealism: Berkeley, scientific realism vs instrumentalism vs van Fraassen's constructive empiricism (15+15 task: explain the contrast, then argue which is more credible), and the experience machine versus reality. Topic 6, consciousness: materialism (reductive, emergent, eliminative) as a 4 p 600-char definition, mind-body, extended mind as a 15+15 task; flag that YTL has credited this to FI1 and FI2 in LOPS19.

Topic 7, sources of knowledge: justification condition, rationalism and empiricism, Montaigne-style scepticism, everyday vs scientific knowledge, testimonial and hermeneutical injustice and prejudice as an epistemic vice. Formats: a two-part 10+10 essay with a short text, a 5+5+20 short-plus-essay and a 20 p everyday-knowledge essay. Topic 8, scepticism and its limits: Montaigne's three stances, fallibilism vs scepticism vs agnosticism; fold it into topic 7 if only ten topics are kept.

Topic 9, scientific reasoning and ethics of science, is the most heavily tested. Carry induction, falsification, demarcation and pseudoscience, hypothetico-deductive method, paradigm, theory-ladenness, criteria (independence, self-correction, progress, criticality), good scientific practice (plagiarism, fabrication, falsification), and science and policy. Formats: a 20-term dropdown matching set (10 x 2 p), a 20 x 1 p multiple choice, a 20 p essay on features of research from a short material, and a 10+5+15 ethics-of-science task. Add pseudoscience as a 5+5+10 task and link to FI1.

Topic 10, explanation and understanding: causal explanation by natural laws vs interpretation, hermeneutic circle, practical syllogism, explanation versus prediction, and how knowledge is formed in history. Formats: dropdown matching including hermeneutic circle and practical syllogism, and a 20 p essay on knowledge formation in a field such as history, with the student's own school studies as material.

Do not copy YTL task text; write original tasks in the same formats and point splits. Keep every FI4 topic's model answer ending with a top-mark note naming one deepening move (another theory, the tradition, or a current example), as YTL does.

Weight the effort: K26 t6 is a 20-item multiple choice and K25 t6 a 20-term matching set, so a glossary-style drill on philosophy-of-science terms is worth building; an extended-mind or consciousness topic is exam-optional by YTL's own LOPS19 mapping, so it can be lighter.

Before building, re-read K23, S23, S24 and K25 grading pages in a browser if a verbatim LOPS19 mapping sentence is needed for the site's curriculum references; those four were read through a summary, and the exact mapping phrase for K23 t6 is unconfirmed. research.versus_expected: The brief's expectation holds: every sitting has FI4 content, covering truth, knowledge, science, language and explanation. Differences from the brief: (1) science and philosophy of science is the dominant strand, in all seven sittings, with scientific realism and anti-realism, Kuhn, Popper and the hermeneutic circle named as terms. The brief lists scientific reasoning only as one topic, and it deserves heavy weight, probably two topics' worth of format variety. (2) Consciousness and mind are marginal: K24 t9 is mapped to FI1 and FI2 only, and FI4 consciousness appears only in K26 t1, S23 t8 and the K26 mapping. research.summary: Neutrality rules for FI4 (Totuus), adapted from contract §C-D and style guide §11-12, §16-17. Two web reads were attempted. The OPH page returned 404 (could_not_read). The media-literacy search returned secondary news only. The rules below therefore rest on the project's own docs (read in full), not on external primary pages. Recommendation: FI4 needs no mandatory safety flag. Death_suicide is optional-by-trigger, and a short content_note is advised only for the consciousness/AI/death-of-self and 'nothing is knowable' scepticism pages if they name death or despair.

findings.claim: Project rules already require: strongest critics presented, no mockery of religious or non-religious views, no political advocacy, tasks never assess the student's beliefs, and 'both sides' never makes curriculum content look optional (contract §C; style guide §11).

Contract §D and style guide §12/16 limit safety_flags to death_suicide and violence; ordinary pages keep a short 'Apua ja tukea' study-help section. No FI4 theme named in the curriculum list (truth, language, necessity, realism, consciousness, knowledge limits, science ethics, explanation) falls in those flag categories by itself.

Rule 1, empirical questions: state settled empirical results (evolution, age of Earth, climate science, vaccine safety, heliocentrism) as findings of science without 'some say / others say'. Symmetry applies only to philosophical questions (realism vs anti-realism, physicalism vs dualism, truth theories). Mark the switch explicitly: 'tämä on empiirinen kysymys, jonka tutkimus ratkaisee' versus 'tämä on filosofinen kysymys, josta kiistellään'.

Rule 2, science and religion: present as different kinds of claim and method, not as winner and loser. Never write that science has refuted religion or that faith is irrational; and never present creationism, astrology or similar as an equal 'alternative' on empirical questions. Pseudoscience is judged by named criteria (testability, falsifiability, peer scrutiny, replication, changing the hypothesis after failure), never by mocking words. A religious claim is analysed as a type of claim (empirical, metaphysical, moral, existential) with the same reporting verbs as any other. Popper's falsifiability and Kuhn are paraphrased, with the demarcation problem named as itself debated, and no single criterion declared final.

Rule 3, relativism and post-truth: separate (a) philosophical relativism about truth or about concepts (analysed with its strongest critics, e.g. self-refutation worry), (b) pluralism of interpretation (legitimate in explanation and understanding, Dilthey), and (c) disinformation (deliberate false claims) and post-truth (appeals to feeling over evidence). Use fictional or historical, dated examples, and no party politics, no named current politicians, no campaigns or elections (FI3 rule §17 applies). Teach evidence-checking criteria (source, evidence, method, correction track record). Do not equate 'truth is contested in philosophy' with 'any claim is as good as another'.

Rule 4, consciousness and AI: frame as an open philosophical and scientific question; present physicalist, dualist and functionalist views with equal length and the same verbs. Do not claim current AI systems are or are not conscious; say what the arguments would require. Use no named company or product claims, no predictions, and no anthropomorphic marketing language. AI used only as thought experiment or concept (Turing, Chinese room named as paraphrased), with dated, linked facts if any capability is stated.

Rule 5, scepticism without nihilism: every scepticism page ends with what survives (fallibilism, degrees of justification, Hume's mitigated scepticism, Descartes' method as a tool), a model answer that ends conditionally, and no wording that tells the student that nothing can be known or that life is meaningless. Radical doubt is presented as a method and a challenge, not a recommended attitude.

Rule 6, no disclosure prompts: tasks use fictional third persons, assigned roles ('puolusta harjoituksena') and arguments, never 'what do you believe'. Reuse the project fail list (itse, perheessäsi, läheisesi, oma uskosi, kerro kokemuksestasi, mihin sinä uskot, kerro ryhmälle) and add FI4 phrases: 'uskotko jumalaan', 'oletko uskonnollinen', 'onko sinulla tietoisuus', 'kerro oma näkemyksesi uskosta'. Pohdinta questions ask about arguments, not the student's own life.

Safety flag decision: no FI4 topic requires safety_flags by default. Conditional: add death_suicide, a content_note and the youth help box only if a page (consciousness/personal identity, death as the end of mind, Epicurus-like arguments, scepticism about the self) discusses death or personal annihilation as a lived question or quotes a text on it. Add violence only if a page names real violence (e.g. a historical example of persecution of heretics or of scientists, such as Galileo's trial or Bruno's execution, if those are used to illustrate science and authority). Concept-level mentions do not trigger flags, per the FI3 precedent. A one-sentence content_note on epistemic or existential anxiety is optional for the scepticism and consciousness pages.

Period-bound and historically charged material: Bacon, Locke, Kant and Dilthey texts contain period-bound views (Kant and Locke on race and on women; Locke on colonies). End excerpts before such passages or add one neutral line within five lines (FI3 pattern). Historical conflict between church and science (Galileo, Bruno, Darwin reception) is told by dated facts from pages a researcher opened, never as 'religion vs science' morality play, and never from memory.

Media-literacy context: Finland has had a national media literacy policy since 2013 (updated 2019) integrated in school subjects. This only supports the framing of FI4's disinformation material as curriculum-consistent, not specific wording. Source was news summaries (secondary).

recommendations: Adopt the six rules above as an FI4 addendum (style guide section 18, contract addendum), keeping section 11 table as the base.

Checker list FAIL: huuhaa, hölynpöly, tiede on kumonnut, uskonto on, 'järjetön usko', 'sokea usko', 'taikausko' as the site's own label, party names and abbreviations, named current politicians, vaalikampanja, hallitusohjelma, äänestä(isit), and disclosure phrases (perheessäsi, läheisesi, oma uskosi, kerro kokemuksestasi, mihin sinä uskot, uskotko jumalaan, oletko uskonnollinen, kerro ryhmälle, kumpaa kannatat). Also fail on claims that a named AI product or company is or is not conscious, and on catastrophe or statistic figures typed from memory.

Checker FLAG REQUIRED (needs safety_flags, content_note, Apua ja tukea): kuolema as lived end of the self, itsemurha, itsetuho, teloitus or polttorovio of a named person, kidutus, vainot. Concept-only uses of kuolema (Epicurus-type argument in logic form) trigger a flag only if the page dwells on personal death.

Checker MANUAL REVIEW: itse, mielestäsi, ainoa oikea, kaikki tietävät, selvästi, ilmeisesti, todellisuudessa and oikeasti (dismissive), väittää, muka, myöntää (asymmetric verbs), 'vain teoria', 'pelkkä mielipide', 'tiede todistaa', 'tiede on todistanut', 'tiede ei voi tietää', 'epätieteellinen' used as insult, 'valeuutinen' without definition, kone ajattelee or tietoinen as unqualified AI claims.

Use the same reporting verbs (sanoo, perustelee) for science, religion, realism and anti-realism; keep opposing philosophical positions within a quarter of each other's length; mark each page's questions as empirical or philosophical.
The neutrality checker should read each model answer for conditional endings and for rewards to one worldview, and confirm scepticism pages end with what survives.
Operator decision: whether a short content_note is wanted on the consciousness and scepticism pages even without a flag; default is no flag, no note unless death or despair is named.

proposal.title: Style-guide section 18: FI4 additions (brief 005), at most 30 lines
proposal.detail:
1. Empirical against philosophical. Settled empirical results (evolution, the age of the Earth, climate science, vaccine safety) are stated as findings, with no 'some say'. Symmetry applies only to philosophical questions. Mark each with 'empiirinen kysymys' or 'filosofinen kysymys'.
2. Pseudoscience is judged by named criteria (testability, falsifiability, replication, peer scrutiny, ad hoc rescue), never by labels such as huuhaa or hölynpöly. The demarcation problem is itself presented as debated.
3. Science and religion are different kinds of claim and method, not winner and loser. Never write that science has refuted religion or that faith is irrational. A religious claim is analysed by type (empirical, metaphysical, moral, existential) with the same verbs as other claims.
4. Relativism, pluralism of interpretation and disinformation are kept distinct. 'Philosophers dispute truth' never means 'every claim is equally good'. Examples are fictional or historical and dated; no parties, current politicians or campaigns (section 17 applies).
5. Consciousness and AI: physicalism, dualism and functionalism get equal length and the same verbs. Never state that a current AI system is or is not conscious. No company or product names, no predictions.
6. Scepticism pages end with what survives: fallibilism, degrees of justification, doubt as method. No wording that says nothing can be known or that life is meaningless.
7. No disclosure prompts. Add to the fail list: uskotko jumalaan, oletko uskonnollinen, kerro oma näkemyksesi uskosta, onko sinulla tietoisuus, kumpaa kannatat.
8. Manual-review words: 'vain teoria', 'pelkkä mielipide', 'tiede todistaa', 'epätieteellinen' used as an insult, 'valeuutinen' without a definition, unqualified 'kone ajattelee'.
9. Non-PD thinkers (Russell, Popper, Kuhn, Quine, von Wright, Hempel, Gettier, van Fraassen) are paraphrased and linked only, never quoted.
10. FI1 overlap: link fi1-06, fi1-08, fi1-09 and fi1-10 instead of re-teaching them. Never re-quote AT VII 18, 27 or 78, Metaphysics 1011b, Enquiry IV or Theaetetus 155d.
11. Formal logic stays light: no symbolic notation in topics 32 and 34; possible worlds are explained in words.
12. Exam formats: every topic has one drill of the kind YTL uses (20 x 1 point choice, 10 x 2 point term matching, or 600-750 character definitions) plus a 20- or 30-point essay.
13. Safety: no default flags. death_suicide applies only if the end of the self is treated as a lived question. violence applies only if a named execution or persecution (Bruno, Galileo's trial) is narrated, and then only from dated pages a researcher opened.
14. Period-bound passages (Locke and Kant on race and women, Bacon on authority) are cut before the excerpt or get one neutral line within five lines.
15. Quotations from Wikisource scan pages strip footnote markers and mark cuts with […].
